literal: Baiyao reached Xianqiu but fell ill and halted.
idiomatic: Baiyao reached Xianqiu, fell ill, and halted.

literal: It happened that Chongji and his younger cousin Fashou seized Song's Panyang city to ransom mother and wife.
idiomatic: Chongji and his cousin Fashou then seized Song's Panyang to ransom mother and wife.

literal: Baiyao sent General Zhangsun Guan and others with cavalry in through Ma'er Pass to go to their aid.
idiomatic: Baiyao sent Zhangsun Guan and cavalry through Ma'er Pass to their aid.

literal: When Guan reached Panyang, all counties submitted.
idiomatic: Guan reached Panyang; every county submitted.

literal: Baiyao advanced from Xianqiu to attack Licheng.
idiomatic: Baiyao advanced from Xianqiu against Licheng.

literal: In year 2 Cui Daogu and Liu Xiubin, garrison chief of Liangzou in Yan Province, both came bound to surrender.
idiomatic: In year 2 Cui Daogu and Yan's Liangzou garrison chief Liu Xiubin came bound to surrender.

literal: Baiyao released them all.
idiomatic: Baiyao released them all.

literal: He sent Daogu, Xiubin, and their staffs to the capital.
idiomatic: He sent Daogu, Xiubin, and their staffs to the capital.

literal: Only afterward were the leading families of the two cities moved to Xiaguan; the court established Pingqi Commandery with counties Huaining and Gui'an to settle them.
idiomatic: Later the leading families of both cities were moved to Xiaguan; the court set Pingqi Commandery with Huaining and Gui'an to house them.

literal: The rest were all made slaves and distributed among the hundred officials.
idiomatic: The rest were enslaved and given to officials.

literal: Though Baiyao was on campaign, he received men with courtesy, broad and kindly.
idiomatic: Though at war, Baiyao received men with broad courtesy.

literal: Chongji's mother and wife and Shen Zuan's women were all quartered separately; he did not let soldiers make uproar.
idiomatic: Chongji's mother and wife and Shen Zuan's women were quartered apart; he kept soldiers from disorder.

literal: When he next took Dongyang, he captured Shen Wenxiu.
idiomatic: When he took Dongyang he captured Shen Wenxiu.

literal: In all they seized eight hundred fifty thousand hu of granary grain.
idiomatic: In all they took eight hundred fifty thousand hu from granaries.

literal: From first to last three years, building siegeworks and attacking—though soldiers died and were wounded, there was little mutiny.
idiomatic: Three years of siege and assault cost many lives, yet little mutiny.

literal: The three Qi districts were glad; people settled and worked in peace.
idiomatic: The three Qi districts were glad; people settled in peace.

literal: On the day the city fell, because Shen Wenxiu stood proud and would not bow, Baiyao in anger had him beaten—only this drew censure.
idiomatic: When the city fell Shen Wenxiu would not bow; Baiyao in anger had him beaten—only this drew blame.

literal: For merit he was appointed Opening the Government with ceremonial rank equal to the Three Excellencies, Commander-in-Chief, Governor of Qing Province, and advanced to Prince of Jinan.
idiomatic: For merit he was made Opening the Government with Three Excellencies' ceremonial rank, Commander-in-Chief, Governor of Qing, and Prince of Jinan.

literal: Earlier, when Yi Hun monopolized power, Baiyao had leaned on him somewhat; later he was blamed for this.
idiomatic: When Yi Hun held sole power Baiyao had leaned on him; later that became his charge.

literal: In year 4 he was executed on the charge of plotting rebellion; opinion at the time called it unjust.
idiomatic: In year 4 he was executed for alleged rebellion; opinion called it unjust.

literal: Baiyao's youngest son Zhen'an, eleven years old, hearing his father was seized, was about to kill himself.
idiomatic: His youngest son Zhen'an, eleven, hearing his father seized, meant to kill himself.

literal: The household stopped him, saying: "The gravity is not yet known."
idiomatic: Kin stopped him: "The charge is not yet known."

literal: Zhen'an said: "A princely rank and weighty merit—if a small fault, it would never come to this.
idiomatic: Zhen'an said: "Prince's rank and great merit—if a small fault, it would never come to this.

literal: I cannot bear to see my father's death."
idiomatic: I cannot bear to see my father die."

literal: He thereupon hanged himself.
idiomatic: He hanged himself.

literal: In the Taihe era Palace Gentleman Author Cheng Yan memorialized in Baiyao's defense; Emperor Xiaowen read it and was moved to pity.
idiomatic: In Taihe Author Cheng Yan memorialized for Baiyao; Xiaowen read it and was moved to pity.

literal: Baiyao's nephew Qi was frivolous and without restraint.
idiomatic: Nephew Qi was frivolous and unrestrained.

literal: At the beginning of Taihe, as a son of a great house he was promoted to Palace Cadet and transferred to Palace Cadet of the Palace Steward.
idiomatic: At Taihe's opening, as a great-house son he became Palace Cadet, then Palace Cadet of the Palace Steward.

literal: Prince of Nan'an Zhen had a reputation for greed and violence; he sent Palace Cadet Lu Wenzu to Chang'an to investigate.
idiomatic: Prince of Nan'an Zhen was known for greed and cruelty; he sent Lu Wenzu to Chang'an to investigate.

literal: Wenzu accepted gold and treasure from Zhen and concealed it without speaking.
idiomatic: Wenzu took Zhen's gold and treasure and concealed the truth.

literal: When the matter broke, the empress dowager received the ministers and said: "Earlier when we discussed greed and purity, all said they could discipline themselves.
idiomatic: When it broke, the empress dowager received the ministers and said: "When we discussed greed and purity, all claimed discipline.

literal: Wenzu was then among them, yet afterward he violated the law.
idiomatic: Wenzu was among them—yet he broke the law.

literal: From this one may say the human heart truly cannot be known."
idiomatic: So the human heart cannot be known."

literal: Emperor Xiaowen said: "If you yourselves judge you cannot overcome greedy hearts, you may resign office and return home."
idiomatic: Xiaowen said: "Who judges himself unable to master greed may resign and go home."

literal: Qi stepped forward and said: "The small man's heart has no fixity, while the emperor's law has constancy.
idiomatic: Qi stepped forward: "The small man's heart has no fixity; the emperor's law is constant.

literal: To serve constant law with an inconstant heart is not what one can bear.
idiomatic: To serve constant law with an inconstant heart is beyond me.

literal: I beg to be dismissed and relieved."
idiomatic: I beg dismissal."

literal: The emperor said: "If Qi knows the heart cannot be constant, he knows the evil of greed—why seek dismissal?
idiomatic: The emperor said: "If Qi knows the heart cannot be constant, he knows greed's evil—why resign?

literal: He was transferred to Director of the Palace Steward and enfeoffed Baron of Dingtao.
idiomatic: He became Director of the Palace Steward and Baron of Dingtao.

literal: Later he died as Commander-in-Chief and Governor of Shuo Province; posthumous title: Victorious.
idiomatic: He later died as Commander-in-Chief and Governor of Shuo; posthumous title: Victorious.

literal: Earlier, after the Murong house was broken, the clan remained numerous.
idiomatic: After the Murong house fell, the clan remained numerous.

literal: At the end of the Tianshi era they were much feared and executed.
idiomatic: At Tianshi's end they were feared and many were killed.

literal: Those who escaped did not dare resume the surname; all took Yu as their clan name.
idiomatic: Survivors dared not resume the surname; all took Yu as clan name.

literal: At the end of Yanchang an edict restored the old surname.
idiomatic: At Yanchang's end an edict restored the old surname.

literal: Yet sons and daughters who had earlier entered the rear palace still bore the name Murong—far more than other clans.
idiomatic: Sons and daughters already in the rear palace still bore Murong—more than any other clan.

literal: Yu Wenfu was of the remote line of the Southern Chanyu.
idiomatic: Yu Wenfu descended from the Southern Chanyu's distant line.

literal: For generations his house were chiefs of the Yong tribe.
idiomatic: For generations his house were chiefs of the Yong department.

literal: His grandfather Huobo served Murong Chui as Inner Secretary of Tang Commandery and Duke of Liaodong.
idiomatic: Grandfather Huobo served Murong Chui as Tang Commandery's inner secretary and Duke of Liaodong.

literal: When Emperor Daowu pacified the Murong house, Huobo entered Wei as the foremost guest.
idiomatic: When Daowu pacified the Murong house, Huobo entered Wei as foremost guest.

literal: Fu in youth was valiant and had strength of body.
idiomatic: Fu in youth was valiant and powerfully built.

literal: In the Taihe era he was repeatedly promoted to Master of Pasturage attendant.
idiomatic: In Taihe he rose to Master of Pasturage attendant.

literal: When the capital moved to Luoyang, an order charged Fu to inspect the horse pastures.
idiomatic: At the move to Luoyang he was ordered to inspect the horse pastures.

literal: Fu marked west of Shiji to east of Henei, a thousand li north and south of the Yellow River, as pasture—the present horse grounds.
idiomatic: He marked west of Shiji to east of Henei, a thousand li along the Yellow River north and south—the present horse grounds.

literal: When mixed herds were moved from Dai to that place, Fu was skilled in tending them and none were lost.
idiomatic: When mixed herds were moved from Dai there, Fu tended them without loss.

literal: Emperor Xiaowen praised him.
idiomatic: Xiaowen praised him.

literal: Shortly he was made Supervisor of the Palace Guard.
idiomatic: Soon he was Supervisor of the Palace Guard.

literal: Later for merit he was enfeoffed Baron of Xiangle and held the posts of Grand Herald, Director of the Department of State Affairs, Grand Umpire of Ying Province, and Governor of Ying Province.
idiomatic: Later for merit he was Baron of Xiangle, then Grand Herald, Director of the Department of State Affairs, Grand Umpire of Ying, and Governor of Ying.

literal: By nature loyal and pure, stern in public office, he ruled men by trust and won great repute.
idiomatic: Loyal and pure by nature, stern in office, he ruled by trust and won great repute.

literal: Later he was made Commander-in-Chief of military affairs at the three garrisons of Huaishuo, Woye, and Wuchuan and Garrison Commander of Huaishuo.
idiomatic: Later he commanded the three garrisons of Huaishuo, Woye, and Wuchuan and was Garrison Commander of Huaishuo.

literal: He died at his post; posthumous title: Loyal and Kind.
idiomatic: He died at his post; posthumous title: Loyal and Kind.

literal: His son Yan, styled Qinghou, had a towering frame and open, sparse brows.
idiomatic: Son Yan, styled Qinghou, was tall and broad, with open, sparse brows.

literal: He held the post of Supernumerary Cavalier Attendant.
idiomatic: He was Supernumerary Cavalier Attendant.

literal: Because his father was old, an edict permitted him to attend and wait in Ying Province.
idiomatic: His father being old, an edict let him wait on him in Ying.

literal: When the Mahayana cultists burst into the prefectural city, Yan led household slaves and guests to meet them in battle and was heavily wounded.
idiomatic: When Mahayana fanatics burst into the city, Yan led slaves and guests to fight and was heavily wounded.

literal: The bandits set fire to the study hall; Fu was then within.
idiomatic: They set fire to the study; Fu was inside.

literal: Yan rushed through the flames, carried Fu out; his limbs were burned raw, hair and temples scorched away.
idiomatic: Yan rushed through flame, carried Fu out; limbs burned raw, hair and temples scorched away.

literal: Thereupon he rallied the host to fight the bandits bitterly; the bandits scattered—for this he won praise.
idiomatic: He rallied men and fought bitterly; the bandits scattered—he won praise for this.

literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Direct Attendant of the Inner Quarters.
idiomatic: He rose to Direct Attendant of the Inner Quarters.

literal: Fighting Wanqi Han the Ghost Slave, he was killed in battle.
idiomatic: Fighting Wanqi Han the Ghost Slave, he fell in battle.

literal: Discussion: Gu Bi's military plans sustained the state and had the measure of a pillar;
idiomatic: Commentary: Gu Bi's stratagems sustained the state—he had a pillar's measure;

literal: Zhang Li was sincere, careful, pure, and square, honored as an old merit-holder.
idiomatic: Zhang Li was sincere, careful, pure, and square, honored among old merit-holders.

literal: Both in a fiber's breadth fell in a single morning.
idiomatic: Both fell in a fiber's breadth in a single morning.

literal: Pardon reaching ten generations—only empty words.
idiomatic: Pardon to ten generations—only empty words.

literal: Liu Jie was a man of blame;
idiomatic: Liu Jie was a man of blame;

literal: Qiu Dui failed and lost his life.
idiomatic: Qiu Dui failed and lost his life.

literal: E Qing and Yi Xu were both employed for strength and talent, while Xu won distinction through stratagem—is he perhaps the better?
idiomatic: E Qing and Yi Xu were used for strength; Xu won distinction by stratagem—perhaps the better?

literal: Yi Gui's fierceness, Zhou Ji's wisdom and courage, Dou Daitian's horsemanship and archery—their appointments were hardly accidental.
idiomatic: Yi Gui's fierceness, Zhou Ji's wit and courage, Dou Daitian's riding and bow—hardly accidental posts.

literal: Che Yiluo's heart dwelt far from common tribesmen—was he merely a routine warrior?
idiomatic: Che Yiluo's heart stood far from common tribesmen—hardly a routine warrior.

literal: Wang Luo'er, Che Lutou, Lu Luyuan, Chen Jian, Lai Dagan, and Su Shi—some with sincerity from the breast, exhausting loyalty in peril;
idiomatic: Wang Luo'er, Che Lutou, Lu Luyuan, Chen Jian, Lai Dagan, Su Shi—some sincere to the bone, loyal in peril;

literal: some guarding the ruler in loyalty, righteousness enough to move men.
idiomatic: some guarding the ruler, righteousness enough to move men.

literal: Had they not been men of fierce will, how could they have done so?
idiomatic: Without fierce will, how could they?

literal: Small wonder they received favor in life and full mourning glory in death.
idiomatic: No wonder they were favored in life and mourned in full glory at death.

literal: As for Anguo, he reached ruin—also the meaning of harm overflowing.
idiomatic: Anguo reached ruin—the meaning of harm overflowing.

literal: Zhou Guan, Wei Bo, Lu Zhen, Lu Luoba, and the rest all advanced through courage and resolution, yet Guan in the end met demotion—different from those several.
idiomatic: Zhou Guan, Wei Bo, Lu Zhen, Lu Luoba advanced by courage; yet Guan was demoted—unlike the rest.

literal: Xue Biaozi carried stern rectitude through generations; Yan Zhen sustained the family name—beautiful, was it not!
idiomatic: Xue Biaozi bore stern rectitude through generations; Yan Zhen sustained the house—beautiful!

literal: Among Wei's generals, regional achievements were rare.
idiomatic: Among Wei's generals, few won regional achievement.

literal: Wei Yuan with his broad, elegant manner undertook command, his prestige reaching far, rank topping the elder statesmen, reaching on his own the place of one who begs to speak—was he not perhaps the one man of recent times!
idiomatic: Wei Yuan's broad, elegant manner bore command; prestige reached far, rank topped the elders, and he won on his own the place of one who begs to speak—perhaps the one man of recent times!

literal: Baiyao went forth on thin campaigns, swept the three Qi, and in reckoning merit on the map his service was no small thing.
idiomatic: Baiyao went forth on lean campaigns, swept the three Qi—in merit reckoned on the map his service was no small thing.

literal: Yet merit and fame are hard to hold; pursued by suspicion he met the blade.
idiomatic: Yet merit and fame are hard to hold; suspicion pursued him to the blade.

literal: Pardoning the worthy and weighing merit—on that day it was not heard.
idiomatic: Pardoning worth and weighing merit—that day it was not heard.

literal: He Qinu's uprightness, Gou Tui's stern rectitude, Yu Wenfu's force of spirit—they too were men of use, were they not!
idiomatic: He Qinu's uprightness, Gou Tui's stern rectitude, Yu Wenfu's force of spirit—they too were useful men!
